title: The ALM Proxy holds the assets while Controllers define the only operations that can touch them
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.3 defines `ALM_CONTROLLER_ROLE` as "the address of the role that can call the `call` functions on the `ALMProxy` contract and update `RateLimits` contract. It includes the `MainnetController` and `ForeignController` contracts. ALM Controller contracts are accessed and modified via the Relayer Role."

The separation of custody from logic is the point. Assets sit in the ALM Proxy, which is a dumb executor: it performs encoded calls handed to it. The Controllers are the only contracts allowed to hand it calls, and each Controller exposes a fixed set of named functions — `mintUSDS`, `burnUSDS`, `swapUSDSToUSDC`, `transferUSDCToCCTP`, deposit and withdraw helpers.

So the Relayer's authority is not "may spend up to X from the treasury." It is "may invoke these specific operations, each with its own preconditions." An operation nobody wrote a Controller function for cannot be performed at all, regardless of how much capacity remains in the rate limits.

This is why adding a venue requires deployment rather than only configuration, and why upgrading a Controller version (Mainnet 1.10, Foreign 1.8) is a governance-relevant event: the Controller *is* the enumeration of what Spark's automation is permitted to do with ecosystem capital.
description: ALM_CONTROLLER_ROLE is the sole caller of the proxy's call functions, and the Relayer acts only through Controllers — so permitted actions are a code whitelist, not a spending allowance.
